correctness.rationale: Fresh exhaustive construction of all 120 permutations gave the exact compatibility graph with 2520 edges and degree 42. An independent Bron-Kerbosch enumeration returned maximal-clique histogram 60 of size 2, 120 of size 3 and 4020 of size 4, with no larger clique. Every one of the 4020 maxima had six pairwise distances exactly three. Explicit construction of all 240 stated isometries verified distance preservation and yielded orbit-size distribution 60x5, 120x7, 240x12. This is exhaustive over the finite graph, not a timeout/sample.

evidence: The foundational paper identifies Ulam/translocation distance and its symmetries.
The later paper develops general finite bounds and states \(A(5,3)=4\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: General coding bounds and the known optimum do not imply the number or orbit structure of all optimum codes.

value.rationale: The parameter cell is a standard small Ulam-code benchmark whose optimum size was known but whose full optimizer landscape was not. A complete exact extremizer census, universal equidistance phenomenon, and symmetry quotient are natural finite classification data that a future coding-theory comparison can directly use.
residual_risks: An unindexed computational enumeration of this small parameter cell could exist, but targeted searches for the exact count, equidistance and orbit profile did not locate one.

final_claim: For Ulam permutation codes in \(S_5\) with minimum distance at least three, there are exactly 4020 labeled maximum size-four codes; every maximum code is pairwise equidistant with all six distances equal to three; under the specified 240-element relabeling-and-reversal isometry subgroup they form exactly 24 orbits, five of size 60, seven of size 120 and twelve of size 240.
limitations: This is a finite classification for \(n=5,d=3\); the 24 orbits are for the explicitly stated 240-element subgroup, not an asserted full isometry group.
An unindexed computational enumeration of this small parameter cell could exist, but targeted searches for the exact count, equidistance and orbit profile did not locate one.
